To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the abundance of resident trout was greater in unconstrained than in constrained reaches of Lookout creek and the presence of rainbow trout depressed juvenile trout abundance in pools with simple habitat structure but not in pools with complex structure.

(a) the geomorphic setting of a stream influences the abundance and distribution of resident trout, (b) the riparian vegetation influences the productivity of a stream and the abundance of trout, and (c) channel morphology influences stream hydraulics, the abundance of trout and the distribution of trout among habitat types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of geomorphic and hydrologic factors on the abundance and distribution of resident salmonids in a small stream.
the influence of channel morphology and riparian characteristics on the distribution and abundance of juvenile and adult salmonids in a small mountain stream in western Oregon.

the influence of channel geomorphology on stream habitat, the influence of stream habitat on fish populations, and the influence of fish populations on the structure and function of riparian communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
geomorphic and riparian factors influence salmonid abundance and distribution in Lookout Creek.
geomorphic influences on the distribution and abundance of salmonids are mediated through their effects on the riparian environment.
geomorphic and riparian influences are important factors in the distribution and abundance of salmonids in streams of the Cascade Mountains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the abundance and distribution of trout in the stream is a product of the interaction among the geomorphic and riparian characteristics that influence stream productivity, habitat structure, and hydraulics.
geomorphologic influences on channel form, and hence habitat, are more important than riparian influences in determining the distribution and abundance of salmonids within stream reaches.
the abundance and distribution of trout is a function of the geomorphic and riparian influences that control habitat structure, stream productivity, and stream hydraulics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salmonid populations are influenced by geomorphic and riparian processes at a variety of scales.
geomorphic context is a major determinant of the abundance of salmonids in stream systems.
the geomorphic and riparian influences on salmonid populations can vary greatly from stream to stream and even from reach to reach.
